choice.candidate: TUI01F (ID/ledger must be checked before future dispatch)
choice.userResult: Explicitly cancel the displayed conversation task from the terminal, then see the same task outcome in the actual Web App and return to the terminal.
choice.whyShortest: One already-published FlowClient.cancel call and durable intent kind; no task body read, center schema, migration, profile, provider or Web renderer change. Manual decisions need a new pending-decision read/detail path; steer has profile/host admission/default-off dependencies and is longer.

currentFacts.evidence: /queue /pause /resume in typed commands; optional QueueControlPort plus center queue capability; version/task bound, one existing intent FSM; explicit recover and page request identity guards.
FlowClient.cancel(taskId,key,signal) POSTs {} to owner /api/tasks/:id/cancel; Web ConversationQueue has separate current-task confirmation. Chat TUI commandSchema has no cancel.
--goal already has /cancel NODE and /decide NODE; do not reuse goal IDs or imply chat controls exist.

No attempt/version parameter in API. Running becomes cancel_requested; unclaimed becomes cancelled; terminal/uncertain/cancel_requested return existing summary. ACK is not proof of actual stop, rollback or native cancellation support.
Task API decide requires pending decisionId and active attempt. Current show returns prompt/entries, so avoid adding that heavy read for the cancel slice.

Conversation capability steer=false; steeringAdmission defaults enabled=false, requires storage/current runner lease/session/profile/host capability and command state. Ordinary profile or catalog does not prove ready. Not part of this slice.

interface.optionalPort: taskControl?: Pick<FlowClient,"cancel"> (one method, absent => UNSUPPORTED_TASK_CONTROL, zero POST)
interface.target: Require opened conversation and taskId equal to its currently displayed current task reference from loaded conversation/queue observation. Freeze conversationId/turnId/taskId/key and input:{} before first POST. Never infer another latest task during recovery. No additional show/prompt read.
interface.intent: Add version-1 task-cancel discriminant alongside unchanged create/send/queue forms; reuse the existing single IntentStore, mutation lifecycle, connection epoch and /recover. A narrow private task-control module owns schema + task-ID/status receipt check, not a new FSM.
interface.ack: Accept only matching task ID and recognized returned task status; clear intent only after matching receipt, then read authoritative conversation/queue. Unknown/transport/malformed ACK retains exact {} / key / task ID. Explicit /recover retries original once, never rebases or substitutes another task.
interface.rejection: Current existing deterministic 4xx behavior preserves draft and refreshes observation without replacement. For cancellation itself there is no queue/task attempt CAS: do not fabricate one. Cross-client stale-CAS proof uses the existing send/queue command.
interface.presentation: Show task ID, scope and distinction between cancel_requested / cancelled / uncertain; do not show success as stopped. Existing shared help/completion and JSONL dispatch expose the command; Ink remains syntax/view only. Ctrl-C and /quit remain observation-only.

noWriteNeeded: existing journal IO or headless implementation

validationIncrement.unitBound: At most 6 targeted task-control/controller cases: missing port, wrong/unobserved task, mismatched ACK, unknown exact-key recovery including original kind journals, late observation/close, terminal/uncertain status truthfulness. No rerun of complete old A-E matrix.
validationIncrement.onePublicFixture: One owned real factory/PG + deterministic fixture runner journey with an HTTP ACK drop proxy: cancel accepted but dropped, close/reopen journal without auto POST, newer second-client changes, explicit /recover original bytes/key and immutable task ID, then current observation. A-to-E existing cases may be reused as provenance, not counted rerun.
validationIncrement.actualPtyAndWeb: One additional shared-center actual Ink PTY + actual production App Chrome journey (can share owned fixture DB/lifecycle): TUI sends initial turn; Web opens same conversation and observes task; Web sends next turn while a controlled read-response barrier leaves TUI revision stale; TUI stale send produces one 409, exact draft remains, observation refreshes and no automatic replacement. After recording preserved draft, explicit user editing invokes /cancel <displayed-task-id>; Web sees request pending then actual fixture cancellation, TUI reconnect sees same IDs/state. No page.reload of user tabs, no DOM injection or HTTP-only substitute for UI clicks.
validationIncrement.exit: Record zero cancel POST for Ctrl-C/disconnect apart from explicit command; cancellation acceptance vs eventual stop is observed separately. A fixture does not prove every native/A2A provider stops.
validationIncrement.distinctEvidence: JSONL/controller verifies public command/intent semantics only. Actual PTY verifies visible typed command, CJK draft, terminal raw-mode/focus/resize/exit. Real Chrome DOM plus request trace proves browser handoff. Only their combined same task/conversation identity earns the narrow TUI-Web-TUI claim.
validationIncrement.performanceAndResource: Record actual request counts/bytes, 0 detail/show/prompt fetch for cancel, bounded existing queue page, journal size unchanged, one current task reference. One random marked DB/dynamic ports/owned process groups; checkpoint evidence before irreversible cleanup. Read-only preparation now, later run requires fresh space >= agreed reserve+fixture/browser allowance; no physical peak assertion.
